_meta.note: The last four how-tos that still admit an honest deterministic proof (the remaining roadmap entries are launch prose). CI0: HeartBeat is CI-usable — exit codes are meaningful, so a pipeline can gate on them (hb audit rejects a hollow DAG non-zero; a good project's exec run exits 0; an unpassable one exits non-zero). EL0: the event log is truth — after a run events.jsonl holds the expected event sequence, every line is valid JSON, and reprojecting the log reproduces the state. EM0: HeartBeat embeds as a library — drive a project via the public API (state.mutate / gate.run_gate / state.project) with no CLI, and a failing gate does not complete. HR0: handle a successful refutation — a review FAIL holds the phase (not completed), then fix + re-gate + a valid distinct-actor review PASS completes it. DW0: the four guides + index + roadmap flips + suite enforcement (T61). Each proof carries a negative/control.

tasks.title: Write ci-flow.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/ci-flow.sh: prove HeartBeat gates a CI pipeline by its exit codes — hb-audit on a hollow DAG exits non-zero (pre-flight catch), a good project driven by a script backend exits 0 from exec run (CI green), and a project whose gate cannot pass exits non-zero (CI red). Print CI-FLOW-OK only when the good flow is 0 and both the hollow DAG and the unpassable gate are non-zero.

tasks.title: Write event-log.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/event-log.sh: complete a phase, then assert events.jsonl is a well-formed authoritative log — every line is valid JSON, the expected events appear in order (initialized, then task_started before task_done before gate_passed), and reprojecting the log reproduces the state (the completed phase). Control: an appended event changes the projection (the log drives state). Print EVENT-LOG-OK only when the sequence, validity, and reprojection all hold.

phases.title: Embed HeartBeat in a Python app

tasks.title: Write embed-python.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/embed-python.sh: drive a project entirely through the Python library API — no CLI subprocess. Using heartbeat.state.mutate / heartbeat.gate.run_gate / heartbeat.state.project, do the work and complete a phase, and assert completed_phases includes it. Control: with the artifact absent the gate does not pass and the phase does not complete (the library gate is real). Print EMBED-PYTHON-OK only when the library-driven run completes and the control holds.

tasks.title: Write handle-refutation.sh
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/gate-examples/handle-refutation.sh: on a review-gated phase whose deterministic gate has passed, record a review FAIL (a found hole) and assert the phase is NOT completed (the refutation held it). Then fix + re-run the gate + record a valid review PASS (a substantive artifact citing the phase, from a DIFFERENT actor than the doer) and assert the phase completes. Print HANDLE-REFUTATION-OK only when the fail holds the phase and the valid distinct-actor pass advances it.

tasks.title: Index + roadmap + enforce
tasks.description: Add the four guides to docs/howto/README.md and flip/add their rows in docs/howto/howto-list.md to the file; add a T61 group to tests/run-tests.sh running the four demos and asserting their markers, so the proofs cannot rot.

GATE_CI0.desc: HeartBeat's exit codes gate a pipeline: hollow DAG and unpassable gate fail; a good flow passes.

review.prompt: Refute that CI0 is done: does it drive the real CLI/auditor? Is each exit-code assertion load-bearing — does the good flow genuinely exit 0 because the gate passed, the hollow DAG exit non-zero from the auditor, and the unpassable gate exit non-zero from exec? Could any be vacuous (e.g. exit 0 for the wrong reason)?

GATE_EL0.desc: The event log is a well-formed authoritative record and the state reprojects from it.

review.prompt: Refute that EL0 is done: are the events genuinely parsed as JSON (not a substring grep)? Is the ordering assertion real (task_started before task_done before gate_passed)? Does reprojecting the log actually reproduce the completed phase (state is derived from the log), and would the proof fail if it didn't?

GATE_EM0.desc: A project runs to completion driven only through the Python library API.

review.prompt: Refute that EM0 is done: does it drive the project through the LIBRARY (state/gate modules), not the CLI subprocess? Does the phase genuinely complete via a real gate run? Is the control load-bearing (with the artifact absent the gate does not pass and the phase does not complete)?

GATE_HR0.desc: A review fail holds the phase; a fix plus a valid distinct-actor review pass advances it.

review.prompt: Refute that HR0 is done: does it drive the real hb CLI review path? Does a review FAIL genuinely hold the phase (not completed)? Does the phase advance only after a VALID review pass — a substantive artifact citing the phase from a DIFFERENT actor than the doer (not a rubber stamp)? Would the proof fail if the fail did not hold or the pass were invalid?

GATE_DW0.desc: Each guide points at a proof that runs; the index and roadmap list all four; the suite enforces the demos.

review.prompt: Refute that DW0 is done: does any guide claim a proof that does not run? Does any restate the enforced mechanisms rather than link them? Are all four guides in the index AND in howto-list.md as created? Does T61 actually run all four demos and assert their markers?

criteria.desc: each guide references its runnable proof
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto" && grep -q 'ci-flow' run-heartbeat-in-ci.md && grep -q 'event-log' read-the-event-log.md && grep -q 'embed-python' embed-heartbeat-in-python.md && grep -q 'handle-refutation' handle-a-successful-refutation.md

criteria.cmd: for f in run-heartbeat-in-ci read-the-event-log embed-heartbeat-in-python handle-a-successful-refutation; do grep -q "$f" "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/README.md" || exit 1; done
